root_cause: The capability gate in build_allocation_plan treats 'llm' as implicitly present by checking required.issubset(capabilities | {'llm'}) and by computing missing_capabilities as required - capabilities - {'llm'}. This allows a node that does not advertise 'llm' to be admitted for tasks requiring it and hides 'llm' from the rejection reason, violating the advertised contract that a node must advertise every required capability.
plan: Remove the implicit 'llm' exemption from the eligibility test so the check is required.issubset(capabilities) with no union.
Update the missing_capabilities calculation to required - capabilities without subtracting {'llm'} so rejections accurately report all missing capabilities.
Ensure rejected entries for capability_mismatch are generated consistently for online nodes and that the rejection reason reflects the true missing set.
Verify the change does not alter handling of blocked/offline nodes and re-run placement logic against tasks with required_capabilities containing 'llm'.
Add explicit tests for nodes lacking 'llm' capability to confirm they are rejected and never recommended.
risks: Placeable count may decrease and previously placed tasks may become blocked if nodes actually lack 'llm' capability.
Existing deployments that relied on the implicit 'llm' exemption could experience allocation failures after the fix.
Changing the rejection record format may affect downstream consumers that expect missing_capabilities to never contain 'llm'.
